text: There is but one God whose name is true, the Creator, devoid of fear and enmity, immortal, unborn, self-existent; by the favour of the Guru. Repeat His name. The True One was in the beginning; the True One was in the primal age. The True One is now also, O Nanak, the True One also shall be.

tags.when_helps: A Sikh or devotional reader seeking a grounding statement of God's eternal nature.

text: By thinking I cannot obtain a conception of Him, even though I think hundreds of thousands of times. Even though I be silent and keep my attention firmly fixed on Him, I cannot preserve silence. Hungry for God, my hunger ceaseth not though I obtain the load of the worlds. If man should have thousands and hundreds of thousands of devices, even one would not assist him in obtaining God. How shall man become true before God? How shall the veil of falsehood be rent? By walking, O Nanak, according to the will of the Commander as preordained.
note: Spiritual longing that thinking and effort can't satisfy

tags.when_helps: A believer frustrated that thinking and effort cannot bring them closer to God.

text: By His order bodies are produced; His order cannot be described. By His order souls are infused into them; by His order greatness is obtained. By His order men are high or low; by His order they obtain preordained pain or pleasure. By His order some obtain their reward; by His order others must ever wander in transmigration. All are subject to His order; none is exempt from it. He who understandeth God’s order, O Nanak, is never guilty of egoism.
note: Accepting a larger order beyond the ego

tags.when_helps: A believer wrestling with why fortunes differ, who finds rest in divine order.

text: The condition of him who obeyeth God cannot be described. Whoever tryeth to describe it, shall afterward repent. There is no paper, or pen, or writer To describe the condition of him who obeyeth God. So pure is God’s name, Whoever obeyeth God knoweth the pleasure of it in his own heart.
note: Inner joy of devotion beyond words

tags.when_helps: A devotional reader moved by the joy of obeying God that words cannot capture.

text: When the hands, feet, and other members of the body are covered with filth, It is removed by washing with water. When thy clothes are polluted, Apply soap, and the impurity shall be washed away. So when the mind is defiled by sin, It is cleansed by the colour of the name. Men do not become saints or sinners by merely calling themselves so. The recording angels take with them a record of man’s acts. It is he himself soweth, and he himself eateth.
note: Guilt, cleansing the mind, and owning your actions

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling stained by wrongdoing who hopes the mind can be made clean again.

text: Pilgrimage, austerities, mercy, and almsgiving on general and special occasions? Whoever performeth, may obtain some little honour. But he who heareth and obeyeth and loveth God in his heart, Shall wash off his impurity in the place of pilgrimage within him. All virtues are thine, O Lord; none are mine. There is no devotion without virtue.

tags.when_helps: A believer questioning whether rituals and almsgiving are enough without love in the heart.

text: Praisers praise God, but have not acquired knowledge of Him, As rivers and streams fall into the sea, but know not its extent, Kings and emperors who possess oceans and mountains of property and wealth! Are not equal to the worm which forgetteth not God in its heart.
note: Humility; wealth is nothing beside a faithful heart

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to value wealth and status above remembrance of God.

text: Make contentment thine earrings, modesty and self-respect thy wallet, meditation the ashes to smear on thy body. Make thy body, which is only a morsel for death, thy beggar’s coat, and faith thy rule of life and thy staff.
note: Inner virtues as the true spiritual discipline

tags.when_helps: A seeker wanting inner virtues, not outward signs, to be the marks of their path.

text: I have no strength to speak and no strength to be silent. T have no strength to ask and no strength to give; I have no strength to live and no strength to die; I have no strength to acquire empire or wealth, which produce 2 commotion in the heart. T have no strength to meditate on Thee or ponder on divine knowledge; T have no strength to find the way to escape from the world. He in whose arm there is strength may see what he can do. Nanak, no one is of superior or inferior strength before God.
note: Feeling powerless; humility before something greater

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels powerless and wants to know that strength is not what matters before God.

text: Make continence Thy furnace, forbearance Thy goldsmith, Understanding Thine anvil, divine knowledge Thy tools, The fear of God Thy bellows, austerities Thy fire, Divine love Thy crucible, and melt God’s name therein. In such a true mint the Word shall be coined.
note: Shaping character through patient spiritual practice

tags.when_helps: A seeker wanting an image of how virtues work together in spiritual life.

text: The air is the Guru, water our father, and the great earth our mother; Day and night are our two nurses, male and female, who set the whole world a-playing. Merits and demerits shall be read out in the presence of the judge. According to men’s acts, some shall be near and others distant from God. Those who have pondered on the name and departed after the completion of their toil, Shall have their countenances made bright, O Nanak; how many shall be emancipated in company with them!
note: Belonging to nature; actions shape our closeness to God

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling kinship with the natural world and mindful that their deeds will count.
